title: Case A: Q3 sales review for the boss
intro:
It's the first week of October. Your manager writes: "Q3 review on Friday. I need two things on one slide: **which region carried Q3**, and **which rep is furthest behind target so far this year**. The system export is attached; it's the usual mess."

This is one piece of work in six steps, the way a real task chains skills: clean → enrich with lookups → pivot → decide → write it up. Each step has its own **Check**, and you can check them in any order. The data decides whether each step is right, so a step built on unclean data fails.

The targets in the Reps table (column T) are **annual**. Three quarters of the year are gone, so the fair comparison is revenue **year to date** (Qtr1–Qtr3) against **¾ of the annual target**.

steps.title: Clean the export
steps.ask: Fix all **11 problems** in the export: duplicates, blank regions, region text, quantities stored as text, the mistyped ProductID, and the date in the wrong year.

defects.label: O1012 Region has stray spaces and lower case
O1140 Region is in lower case
O1045 Quantity is stored as text
O1150 Quantity is stored as text
O1088 ProductID has a letter O instead of a zero
O1170 is dated 2026: a typo for 2025

steps.hint: The same six moves as Assignment 3. Check the pivot's note for product IDs that aren't in the price list.

solution.explain: Remove Duplicates · rep lookup into the blank Regions · TRIM(PROPER()) down D · Convert to Number on G · P0O2 → P002 · O1170's date → 2025-12-12.

steps.title: Enrich: one order's revenue
steps.ask: Order **O1088** was the one with the mistyped ProductID. Find its row, then work out its **revenue** with a lookup: Quantity × ListPrice × (1 − Discount). Type it in the box and press **Run**.
steps.hint: If the lookup says #N/A, the ProductID is still mistyped: that's why cleaning comes first.

steps.title: Pivot: Q3 revenue by region
steps.ask: Build a pivot of **revenue by region for Qtr3 only** (filter the quarter), on the cleaned data.
steps.hint: Rows: Region; Values: Sum of Revenue; Filter: Quarter = Qtr3. If you inserted the pivot before cleaning, Refresh it.

steps.title: Pivot: revenue by rep, year to date
steps.ask: Now switch the pivot to **revenue by rep, year to date**: Qtr1, Qtr2 and Qtr3 (not Qtr4).
steps.hint: Rows: Rep; Filter: Quarter with Qtr1–Qtr3 ticked and Qtr4 unticked.

steps.title: Enrich: a target to date
steps.ask: Look up **Maria Ioannou**'s annual Target in the Reps table and take **¾** of it: her target to date. Type it in the box and press **Run**.
steps.hint: Search RepName (Q), return Target: it's the 4th column of Q:T. Then × 0.75.

steps.title: The two-sentence finding
steps.ask: Chart the pivot that makes your point (columns or bars, largest first), then complete the finding. Work out each rep's year-to-date revenue as a % of ¾ of their target: the lowest is not necessarily the rep with the least revenue.

story.sentence: In Q3, {region} brought in the most revenue (€{regionAmount}), just ahead of {runnerUp}. Against target to date, {rep} is furthest behind at {repPct}% of target, even though {lowest} brought in less.

repPct.label: their % of target to date (1 decimal)

regionAmount.label: Q3 revenue of the top region

steps.hint: Q3 region figures come from the Qtr3 pivot. For the reps: year-to-date revenue ÷ (Target × 0.75), for each rep; the smallest % is furthest behind.

story.title: Giorgos Nikolaou is furthest behind target

claimAfter: I can take a messy export to a short, correct finding for a manager: cleaned, enriched, pivoted and checked against targets.
